name: Sodium bicarbonate
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Sodium bicarbonate is an alkalinizing agent; the bicarbonate is handled by the kidney and lungs, so there is no kidney dose reduction. The kidney concern is the sodium load: the US label (isotonic IV solution) asks for monitoring for fluid overload in kidney disease and anuria, plus electrolytes to avoid alkalosis and hypernatremia. Oral tablets used for the metabolic acidosis of CKD are outside this label; KDIGO 2024 suggests considering treatment when serum bicarbonate is below 18 mmol/L, without overshooting the upper limit of normal.
kidney_function_basis: Not applicable: dosing is by acid-base status, not kidney function.

bands.recommendation: IV for metabolic acidosis (adults and children 2 years and older): 2 to 5 mEq/kg over 4 to 8 hours, by bicarbonate, total CO2, pH and clinical state (label). Treat the cause.

No kidney dose change in the label. Kidney disease and anuria increase sensitivity to the sodium load: watch for fluid overload, edema and blood pressure, and adjust other sodium sources (label 5.1). Monitor bicarbonate, sodium and potassium; avoid overshoot alkalosis. Oral tablets for CKD metabolic acidosis: consider treatment to keep serum bicarbonate from falling below 18 mmol/L, and do not overshoot the upper limit of normal; watch blood pressure, potassium and fluid status (KDIGO 2024 PP 3.10.1, 3.10.2). Each 650 mg tablet supplies about 7.7 mEq of sodium and bicarbonate (325 mg about 3.9 mEq); 8.4% solution is 1 mEq/mL (84 mg per mEq; label 3: 12.6 mg/mL = 0.150 mEq/mL). Oral doses are not in the label.

hd.text: No dose change; anuria raises the risk of fluid overload from the sodium load (label 5.1). Dialysate bicarbonate also corrects acidosis; coordinate with the dialysis prescription (clinical judgment).
hd.short: No dose change; fluid overload risk

pd.text: No dose change; watch sodium load and fluid status (label 5.1).
pd.short: No dose change; watch sodium load

crrt.text: No data in label. CRRT fluids are usually bicarbonate-buffered; added IV bicarbonate is a specialist decision guided by blood gases.

dialyzable: Bicarbonate crosses dialysis membranes in both directions according to the dialysate bicarbonate concentration (physiology; not stated in label).
monitoring: Blood gases or serum bicarbonate, sodium, potassium (hypokalemia as acidosis corrects), fluid status, blood pressure, edema. Extravasation site (hypertonic solutions).

pediatric.usual_dose: 2 years and older: 2 to 5 mEq/kg over 4 to 8 hours. Under 2 years and neonates: 1 to 2 mEq/kg over 4 to 8 hours; avoid rapid or bolus doses (label).
pediatric.max_dose: Under 2 years: rate no more than 8 mEq/kg/day (label 8.4).
pediatric.neonates: 1 to 2 mEq/kg over 4 to 8 hours; no more than 8 mEq/kg/day; rapid injection risks hypernatremia and intracranial hemorrhage (label).

adult: Selected US label is an isotonic 1.26% (0.150 mEq/mL) premixed bag (Baxter, 2026). PH registers 8.4% (1 mEq/mL) ampoules/vials (38 products) and 325 or 650 mg tablets (29). The 8.4% hypertonic solution carries more extravasation and hypernatremia risk; consider pinning an 8.4% US label as an alternate.
Dialyzability line is general physiology, labelled as such.

revision_log.change: KDIGO 2024 PP 3.10.1–3.10.2 added for oral tablets in CKD G3–G5 (bicarbonate ≥18 mmol/L, not above upper limit of normal; watch BP, potassium, fluid). mEq per tablet computed from the label's 84 mg per mEq ratio.
